focus: Q1 and Q2: map every surface that decides packet placement and what relatedness signal each one already has.
answeredQuestions: Q1: At the moment an agent decides where new work goes (Gate 3 prompt text, gate-3-classifier.ts, the Gate 3 runtime hook, /speckit:plan setup), does anything surface the series parent rule or the sibling packets, and where are the gaps that still let a related singleton be created?

Q2: Which existing mechanisms already compute relatedness (gate-3-classifier, folder-routing, the trigger index and lookup, the skill advisor, recommend-level.sh, graph-metadata) and which could detect a same-artifact sibling mechanically instead of relying on the agent to read stderr?

label: The runtime Gate 3 menu the operator answers never names the series parent and lists no siblings: GATE_3_QUESTION option C is 'Use a related spec folder, including a phase child', the mutation notice repeats the same gap, and the Pi dialog label is 'Use a related folder or phase child', while only AGENTS.md prose carries the series-parent clause.

The classifier and binding validation are structural, never relational: ClassificationResult has no placement or relatedness fields, GATE_3_VOCABULARY holds only four trigger categories, and validateSpecFolderBinding checks path resolution, mandatory metadata and the NNN-name shape, so a related singleton answer binds with no warning.

The /speckit:plan and /speckit:complete command assets carry no series-parent wording; a case-insensitive search for 'series' across .skilled/commands returns zero hits, the confirmation line reads 'Q1. Spec Folder: A) Use existing B) Create new C) Related D) Skip documentation', and Option C appears in the YAML only for phase-child spec_id derivation. This contradicts the strategy section 12 claim that the plan/complete YAML shipped the wording.

The only sibling-surfacing mechanism runs post-decision and filtered: list_recent_track_packets is called only from resolve_branch_name during scaffolding, lists top-level NNN- folders only, requires graph-metadata derived.created_at (skipping packets without it), applies a 14-day cutoff and a 10-row cap, prints name/date/100-char description to stderr, and never compares the new work against the listed rows.

Five relatedness-capable mechanisms exist but none carries an artifact key: folder-routing alignment score (save-time, folder-name words, prints better alternatives), trigger-index phrase scoring with a --spec-folder scope filter returning document paths, track graph-metadata children_ids/parent_id sibling enumeration plus manual opt-in depends_on/related_to/supersedes, phrase-judge phrase-quality classes, and no relatedness in recommend-level.sh or skill-advisor (routes prompts to skills, not packets).

The Gate 3 question text is byte-pinned: delivery-receipt tests assert byteCount equals Buffer.byteLength(GATE_3_QUESTION), a test freezes byte-identical baseline output, and the question hash is computed through the canonical policy block with GATE_SPEC_FOLDER_QUESTION_ID, so any menu-wording fix must move the runtime copies and these hashes/tests together.

Two canon copies of the option menu already drift: AGENTS.md option C contains the series-parent clause while the runtime GATE_3_QUESTION and dialog labels do not; the strong rule lives in prompt prose and the weak menu is what gets answered.
